title: Regional Manthan Conference on Road Safety
body_text:
The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) today organised a Regional Manthan Conference to deliberate on strengthening road safety through e-Enforcement, integrated data systems, safer vehicles, improved emergency response and stronger district-level capacity for western states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and Union Territory of Dadra Nagar Haveli and Daman Diu (DNH & DD) at Mumbai under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Justice A M Sapre [Retd.], Chairman Supreme Court  Committee on Road Safety. Shri Sanjay Bandyopadhyay Member SCCORS and Shri Mahmood Ahmed AS(T), MoRTH along with other senior officials also attended the conference. The following were deliberated in detail during conference: -
Zero Fatality District Initiative: Targeting Where It Matters Most
Good intentions and good schemes must be directed with precision. The Zero Fatality District (ZFD) initiative is our strategic response to the question: where do we act first, and how do we act comprehensively? The ZFD model has been expanded nationally, with 100 critical districts identified across 15 states for focused, 360-degree intervention combining engineering, enforcement, emergency care, and education. These 100 districts together recorded with an average of 400+ fatalities per district annually . The ZFD framework, tailored to each district's specific crash profile, offers a proven strategy to achieve substantial fatality reduction.
B.        PM Rahat: No Victim Should Be Lost for Want of Care
Research tells us that 50% of fatalities can be averted if the victim is admitted to hospital within the first one hour i.e., the Golden Hour. And yet, across our country, victims lie unattended, families scramble for cash, and hospitals hesitate to act without assurance of payment. The PM Rahat Scheme , is our definitive response to this tragedy.
PM Rahat provides cashless treatment of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for up to 7 days from the date of accident, covering all road accident victims irrespective of insurance status. What makes this scheme genuinely transformative is its technology backbone including the seamless integration of eDAR (MoRTH) with TMS 2.0 (NHA) , the linkage with the 112 emergency helpline . For the first time, Transport, Health, and Police are working from the same data, in real time, toward the same outcome i.e., no victim is lost due to a delay in care.
C.        Rah-Veer: Honoring the Courage of the Good Samaritan
Even the best emergency care system cannot function if no one acts in those first critical moments at the scene of an accident. This is where the Rah-Veer scheme enters. Rah-Veer is the Government of India's formal recognition and reward for Good Samaritans i.e., individuals who, in the face of uncertainty and risk, choose to stop and save a life by rushing the accident victim to hospital within the Golden Hour.
Every Rah-Veer who saves a life in a serious accident including one involving major surgery, brain or spinal cord injury, at least three days of hospitalization, or death during treatment, is entitled to a cash award of Rs. 25,000 per incident , accompanied by a Certificate of Appreciation. Critically, these Good Samaritans are also protected by law i.e., no Rah-Veer can be subjected to legal proceedings without their consent. Together, PM Rahat and Rah-Veer create a complete emergency care chain i.e., from the moment of accident to the moment of full recovery.
D.        Sadak Suraksha Mitra: Building a Community of Road Safety Champions
Road accident statistics reveal that individuals in the age group of 18–45 years account for 66.1% of all fatalities, underscoring the urgent need to involve youth in road safety initiatives. With this objective, the Sadak Suraksha Mitra (SSM) Programme was launched as a youth-led road safety initiative jointly conceptualised by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports.
The programme seeks to strengthen district-level road safety interventions by engaging trained youth volunteers through the MYBharat platform, with a special focus on the top 100 high-fatality districts across the country, where District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) serve as the primary governance mechanism. These volunteers are not passive bystanders; they are structured road safety professionals, assuming defined roles as Crash Scene Coordinators, data collection for Road Safety Auditors, and Awareness & Engagement Leads. Each role contributes to a specific dimension of district-level road safety action, thereby creating a cadre of youth leaders dedicated to reducing fatalities and promoting safer roads.
E.        Data-Driven Hyperlocal Interventions: The Science Behind the Solution
Knowing where accidents happen is only the first step. Acting on that knowledge systematically, at scale, and with the right tools is the harder challenge. The Data-Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI) framework, is built precisely for this purpose. DDHI empowers District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) to move from intuition-based planning to evidence-based action.
The DDHI roadmap follows a structured five-stage cycle: Alignment Meeting, Capacity Building, Interventions Planning, Implementation, and Impact Assessment . Each district begins with an alignment on programme objectives, moves through capacity building that deskills processes and upskills people, and proceeds to the identification and implementation of hyperlocal interventions suited to that district's unique crash profile.
These five programmes are not just isolated efforts. They are interlocking pieces of a single, coherent road safety architecture . Community engagement through SSM feeds into district planning, data intelligence directs enforcement and engineering, Good Samaritans bridge the gap to emergency care and cashless treatment ensures that no Golden Hour is wasted. Hence, every State and district official were urged to take the insights of this workshop back to the field, and integrate these programmes into your road safety plans.
The Conference reaffirmed that reducing road fatalities requires coordinated action across technology, enforcement, vehicle safety, emergency care, crash investigation and institutional capacity.
States and districts were urged to translate these discussions into time-bound action on the ground, strengthening enforcement and road safety systems towards the goal of safer roads and Zero Fatality Districts.
At the end of the conference, it was agreed that States will due root cause analysis of road fatalities, prepare action plan to reduce road accidents and fatalities, prepare District Road Safety Plan to achieve India’s goal of reducing road fatalities by 50% by 2030.
*****
GDH/DS

enrichment.summary: MoRTH's Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety, chaired by Justice A M Sapre, held a Regional Manthan Conference in Mumbai for Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and DNH & DD to review road safety initiatives. The conference discussed the Zero Fatality District (ZFD) initiative covering 100 high-fatality districts, the PM Rahat cashless treatment scheme, the Rah-Veer Good Samaritan award scheme, the Sadak Suraksha Mitra youth volunteer programme, and the Data-Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI) framework. States were asked to prepare District Road Safety Plans to help India achieve its goal of reducing road fatalities by 50% by 2030.
enrichment.context: India has among the highest road accident fatality numbers globally, and reducing this toll by 50% by 2030 (aligned with the UN Decade of Action for Road Safety and the Brasilia/Stockholm Declarations) has been a stated government goal since the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, and the National Road Safety Policy. The Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety (SCCoRS), constituted following judicial directions, monitors implementation across states. This conference consolidates several distinct but interlinked interventions: the Zero Fatality District programme applies a 4E approach (engineering, enforcement, emergency care, education) to the worst-affected districts; PM Rahat and Rah-Veer together aim to operationalise the 'Golden Hour' concept by ensuring victims get free emergency treatment and by incentivising bystanders to help without fear of legal harassment (building on a 2016 Supreme Court directive protecting Good Samaritans); Sadak Suraksha Mitra leverages the MY Bharat youth volunteer platform; and DDHI institutionalises evidence-based, data-driven local planning. Collectively these reflect a shift from generic road-safety messaging toward district-specific, data-backed, multi-agency (Transport-Health-Police) convergence, integrating databases like eDAR and TMS 2.0.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

prelims_questions.question: With reference to India's road safety initiatives, consider the following statements: 1. The PM Rahat Scheme provides cashless treatment up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for road accident victims irrespective of insurance status. 2. The Rah-Veer Scheme provides legal immunity to Good Samaritans who assist accident victims without their consent being required for legal proceedings. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PM Rahat covers cashless treatment up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for 7 days for all victims regardless of insurance status, and Rah-Veer protects Good Samaritans from legal proceedings without their consent, so both statements are correct.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Golden Hour' concept in the context of road accident emergency care refers to which of the following?
options: The first hour after an FIR is registered for a road accident
The first hour after an accident, within which timely medical care can significantly reduce fatality risk
The first hour of a road safety audit conducted by district authorities
The first hour after a driver's licence is issued
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that research shows 50% of fatalities can be averted if the victim receives hospital care within the first hour after an accident, known as the Golden Hour.

mains_questions.question: India has committed to reducing road accident fatalities by 50% by 2030. Discuss the key institutional and technological interventions introduced by the Government to achieve this target, and examine the challenges in their district-level implementation.

'Good Samaritan' protection is essential to improving emergency response in road accidents in India. Critically examine the legal and policy measures taken to encourage bystander assistance to accident victims.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

study_notes.reason: The release carries specific, testable scheme parameters (PM Rahat's Rs 1.5 lakh cashless cover, Rah-Veer's Rs 25,000 award, ZFD's 100-district count) alongside genuine analytical material on India's evidence-based, multi-agency road safety architecture and its 2030 fatality-reduction target, making it equally useful for memorisation and for argument-building.

prelims.point: Zero Fatality District (ZFD) initiative covers 100 critical districts across 15 states, using a 4E approach: engineering, enforcement, emergency care, and education.
prelims.why_important: UPSC could test the number of districts, states covered, or the four components of the 4E framework.

prelims.point: Sadak Suraksha Mitra (SSM) is a youth-led road safety programme jointly conceptualised by MoRTH and the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, operating through the MY Bharat volunteer platform.
prelims.why_important: Tests the inter-ministerial nature of the scheme and its delivery platform, a common prelims distinction point.

prelims.point: The Data-Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI) framework follows a five-stage cycle: Alignment Meeting, Capacity Building, Interventions Planning, Implementation, and Impact Assessment.
prelims.why_important: The sequential stages of a named framework are exactly the kind of list UPSC converts into a matching or sequencing question.

mains.point: PM Rahat and the eDAR-TMS 2.0-112 data integration operationalise the 'Golden Hour' concept by making Transport, Health and Police work off shared real-time data.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on strengthening India's post-accident trauma care system and inter-agency data convergence in public service delivery.

mains.point: 66.1% of road fatalities occur in the 18-45 age group, justifying a youth-centred intervention strategy like Sadak Suraksha Mitra.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on targeting policy interventions using demographic data and engaging youth in public safety governance.

mains.point: States are being asked to prepare District Road Safety Plans as the operational mechanism to meet India's goal of halving road fatalities by 2030.
mains.theme: Federal implementation of national safety targets
mains.analytical_use: Deployable in questions on Centre-State coordination mechanisms and India's commitments under the UN Decade of Action for Road Safety.

both.concept: PM Rahat (cashless treatment up to Rs 1.5 lakh for 7 days, irrespective of insurance) combined with Rah-Veer (Rs 25,000 award and legal protection for Good Samaritans) forms an integrated emergency-care-to-recovery chain.
both.prelims_angle: Specific figures, eligibility conditions, and the legal protection clause for Good Samaritans can be tested as factual statements.
both.mains_angle: Illustrates how policy design addresses behavioural (bystander fear of legal harassment) and financial (upfront treatment cost) barriers to effective emergency response.

low_priority.point: Names and designations of attending officials such as Sanjay Bandyopadhyay and Mahmood Ahmed.
low_priority.reason: Personnel attendance at a conference has no examinable value.

low_priority.point: The regional scope of the conference (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, DNH & DD).
low_priority.reason: Administrative detail about a single regional event, not a testable fact of national significance.
